selections.comment: LIEUTENANT LILY debuts in a handicap off a very workable mark. The daughter of Cracksman outran odds of 33/1 to finish a respectable third in a novice race over 1m2f at Goodwood most recently, where the fitting of a tongue-tie was instrumental in that improved effort. With the application retained and the step up in trip a source of progression, Tom Ward's filly looks worth chancing in a wide-open finale. The Godolphin-owned pair Dangerman and Desert Shadow both command respect, while Sudu and Vilaine Verlaine can also figure.

selections.comment: It's worth chancing PARAGON can open his account having been dropped a pound by the assessor for a placed effort last time. The first two home over a mile at Chepstow then probably enjoyed a bit of an advantege having raced close to the near rail (likewise the fourth) and Paragon lacked a gear to get on terms. With the extra two furlongs likely to play to his strengths he looks the answer. Penn Avenue, like the selection also making her Polytrack debut, looks a big threat. A very encouraging second on season debut in April, she then disappointed when sent off favourite at Bath upped to this trip last time. There were some excuses for that below par effort (firm ground and lack of racing room) and another crack at this trip is well worth a go. If bouncing back she will prove a real danger. Herkeios has claims on the pick of his recent form but Harryella is next on the list having gone well back from a layoff last time on the back of a course win over 1m in December and looks to hold every chance of staying upped again in trip

Hampered at the start and then forced to wait for a room as the race truly developed better still can be reasonably expected (some novice/maiden form last year promised a fair bit more). Now he's back on track he can break his duck and land this. Kessaar Power, a course and distance winner last October, is entitled to go close on the pick of his form and should bounce back now returned to more favourable conditions and looks the main threat ahead of Tactical Control, Saved Lizzie and Laurentia. Marginal preference of that trio is for Tactical Control who can be reasonably excused his last two efforts and was knocking on the door prior to those, including over course and distance in March

The biggest query is over the trip but given the manner of his win over 6f the extra furlong should be well withinn his compass. The main threat could come from Rapido Girl who wasn't beaten far when fourth two days ago at Catterick in a class 5 handicap. There's a chance she's a bit better at Catterick than elsewhere (her only win came there too) and she's yet to be tested on Polytrack but on balance she's entitled to prove a real handful if no worse for wear for her recent effort. Thomas Equinas is next on the short-list despite the slight rise in class, just ahead of H Key Lails and Nubough

Prior to that run he got within 1/2l of the French Guineas winner over C&D and likely has more to offer with Moore taking over. Recent Owenstown Stud Stakes winner Copacabana Sands is also feared as she isn't fully exposed and gets weight from all.
